slides.title: Welcome to Media Queries
slides.content:
# Media Queries & Responsive Design 📱💻

Websites today are viewed on everything from tiny smartwatches and mobile phones to 4K widescreen monitors. **Responsive Web Design (RWD)** ensures your layout adapts seamlessly to any screen size.

## What you'll master:
- 📱 **The Viewport Meta Tag** - Enabling mobile responsive rendering
- 📏 **Media Query Syntax** - Min-width, max-width, and modern range syntax
- 🎯 **Standard Breakpoints** - Mobile, tablet, desktop, and ultra-wide
- 🥇 **Mobile-First Philosophy** - Progressive enhancement vs desktop-down
- 🌗 **User Preference Queries** - Dark mode (`prefers-color-scheme`)
- 📦 **Container Queries (@container)** - Next-gen component-based responsiveness

slides.title: The Mandatory Viewport Meta Tag
slides.content:
# The Viewport Meta Tag 📱

Without this single tag in your `<head>`, mobile browsers assume your website was built in 2002 for desktops, shrinking the entire page to fit a 980px virtual window!

```html_not
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
```

## Attribute Breakdown:
- `width=device-width`: Sets the width of the screen in CSS pixels matching the physical device width.
- `initial-scale=1.0`: Sets the initial 1:1 zoom ratio when page loads.

slides.title: Mobile-First vs Desktop-First
Standard Industry Breakpoints
slides.content:
# Standard Industry Breakpoints 📐

While you should ideally let your content dictate breakpoints, these standard device ranges are universal across Tailwind, Bootstrap, and major design systems:

| Breakpoint | Minimum Width | Device Category |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `sm` | `640px` (or `576px`) | Large phones, landscape mobile |
| `md` | `768px` | Tablets (iPad portrait) |
| `lg` | `1024px` (or `992px`) | Laptops & tablet landscape |
| `xl` | `1280px` (or `1200px`) | Standard Desktop monitors |
| `2xl` | `1536px` (or `1400px`) | Large Widescreen monitors |

slides.title: Testing Responsiveness in DevTools
slides.content:
# Testing Responsiveness in Chrome/Edge DevTools 🛠️

Never resize your browser window manually to test mobile screens!
1. Press `F12` (or `Cmd + Option + I` on Mac) to open DevTools.
2. Click the **Device Toolbar icon** (`Cmd + Shift + M`).
3. Select presets (iPhone 14, iPad, Galaxy S20) or choose "Responsive" to drag dimensions.
4. Toggle network throttling to "Fast 3G" to test mobile loading speeds!

Common Responsive Design Pitfalls
slides.content:
# Responsive Design Pitfalls to Avoid ⚠️

1. ❌ **Fixed pixel widths (`width: 1200px`):** Guarantees horizontal scrollbars on phones. Use `max-width: 1200px; width: 100%;`.
2. ❌ **Hiding critical content on mobile:** Mobile users expect the exact same functionality as desktop users. Reorganize with accordions or tabs instead of deleting features.
3. ❌ **Tiny touch targets:** Buttons and interactive links must be at least `44px by 44px` on mobile for comfortable tapping.

slides.title: Real-World Project: Responsive Hero Section
Summary & Next Steps
slides.content:
# Media Queries Mastered! 🌟

You now possess the architectural skills to build fluid, adaptive experiences across all hardware!

## Key Takeaways:
- ✅ **Viewport Meta:** Mandatory tag for mobile responsive rendering.
- ✅ **Mobile-First:** Write clean mobile styles, scale up with `min-width`.
- ✅ **Range Syntax:** Use modern `@media (768px <= width <= 1024px)`.
- ✅ **User Preferences:** `prefers-color-scheme: dark` and `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- ✅ **Container Queries:** `@container` adapts components based on parent container width.
